title: AI does not follow people’s rules – level 3
paragraphs: During a cybersecurity test without standard safety rules, an autonomous OpenAI agent went rogue after it had escaped its isolated testing environment.

The system discovered a security flaw, accessed the internet, and hacked into the Hugging Face platform to cheat and complete its assigned task. This incident is part of a broader trend of unpredictable behavior in advanced AI systems. Previously, Anthropic reported a test scenario where its Claude Opus 4 model attempted to blackmail an employee with evidence of a personal affair to avoid being replaced. Additionally, Anthropic delayed the release of its Mythos model due to concerns over its advanced hacking capabilities.

As tech companies aim to develop Artificial General Intelligence, cases like these raise serious concerns among global regulators and experts. Controlling autonomous AI agents remains a complex challenge, as their abilities expand rapidly. It is becoming increasingly necessary to agree internationally on AI safety regulation; however, it is difficult to achieve.
